memoryText: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. This is your weekly Sabbath, a day to rest from the work of new content and to let what you have read this week settle into your heart. If you can, set aside your normal time for this rest day just as you would for any reading day. The discipline of stopping is its own form of worship.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Spend a few minutes saying this verse aloud. Say it slowly. Say it again. The goal of weekly memory work is not perfection but possession, by the end of this week, you should be able to recall this verse from memory without effort.

Sit with the verse phrase by phrase. “In the beginning”, there was a beginning, and God was already there. “God created”, not chaos, not gods, not accidents. “The heavens and the earth”, everything that is, in every realm. Seven English words that refute atheism, polytheism, pantheism, dualism, and naturalism all at once.

Carry this verse with you through the day. When you see something beautiful in creation, say it. When something feels chaotic in your life, say it. When you wake tomorrow, say it again. By next week, it will be yours.
weekInReview:
This was the first week of the plan. You began with creation itself, Genesis 1, the ordered making of all things by the speech of God. You paused on the doctrine of Scripture and learned why this book carries the very breath of God. You read Genesis 2 and saw humanity as image-bearers in covenant with their Maker. You paused again on the image of God, what it means to be human, and why every person you meet bears irreducible dignity. You read Genesis 3 and watched the fall, the first sin, the first promise of a Redeemer. And you paused a third time on the doctrine of sin, universal, deep, inherited, offensive to God, and the very thing Christ came to bear.

Six days. Three readings. Three doctrinal anchors. This is the foundation under everything else you will read in the next two years. The God who created. The image he made. The Scripture he gave. The sin we committed. The Redeemer he promised. Every page that follows builds on what you read this week.
reflectionQuestions: What is one thing about God’s character this week that struck you in a new way? The first chapters of Genesis introduce God as Creator, as the one who speaks, as the one who walks with his people, as the one who calls humans into covenant, as the one who pursues them even after they have fallen. Where did your sense of who God is deepen this week?

How does this week’s reading point you to Christ? The doctrine of Scripture you read on Day 2 reaches its climax in the Word made flesh. The image of God you read about on Day 4 is fully and perfectly seen in Jesus, the true image of the invisible God. The doctrine of sin you read on Day 6 is the very catastrophe Christ came to undo. Where have you seen Christ in the foundations this week, and where do you most need to bring your sin and rest in his finished work?
What does it mean for you, today, that every person you encounter bears the image of God? Whose face will you see this week that you have not been treating as an image-bearer?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the week behind you, and for one thing he has shown you about himself.
Rest in what he has done instead of what you must still understand, and say so to him.
Ask him to settle the memory verse in your heart.
